messages:
sara: thinking out loud — can we move to a telemetry-driven gate for model intake instead of running the full bench on every commit? my rough idea: run a tiny golden set + a long-tail sampler that updates continuously and only trigger full bench on distribution drift or perf delta > X.

ben: I like that. reduces cost and surfaces real regressions. two quick notes: 1) the long-tail sampler needs reproducible seeds+tags so we can backfill. 2) we should keep a small reservoir of ‘rare’ inputs (hard examples) pinned to each model family.

ada: question — how do you define "distribution drift" here? KL on token-lm distribution? or something simpler like response-length + latency histograms? false positives will kill velocity.

ben: start simple: monitor per-route p95 latency, avg token-rate, and a KL on embedding space for a small sample (50-200 examples/day). if any metric crosses threshold -> enqueue full bench. thresholds should be tunable per-customer/tier.

ada: tunable thresholds + a rolling window makes sense. also: add a stability penalty so a single blip doesn't trigger expensive runs. maybe require 3 consecutive windows or a sustained 6h drift.

sara: agree on the hysteresis. operationally: where does this live? in the intake service or as a post-ingest telemetry job?

dave: put the gate logic in the intake coordinator but feed it signals from telemetry-store. flow: ingest -> light smoke (golden + sampler) -> telemetry written -> gate evaluates -> either auto-schedule full bench or mark model green. keeps decision co-located with intake but decouples compute.

michelle: retention/tracking question — if we sample long-tail continuously we need to store provenance: model-commit, seed, input-hash, output-hash, and perf-metrics. storage costs add up. propose compact provenance and periodic backfill instead of full retention.

ben: example compact schema we used elsewhere: 6 fields — model_id, commit_hash, sample_id, input_bucket, small-metrics-json, repro-seed. compressed newline-delimited JSON works.

ben: snippet for sampling config prototype:
```json
{
  "sampler": "stratified",
  "buckets": ["common","rare","user-reported"],
  "rate": {"common": 0.01, "rare": 0.5, "user-reported": 1.0},
  "repro_seed_policy": "daily-rotating"
}
```

ada: also recommend a synthetic-fuzz pass for agent/edge-cases — small (1000) corpus run monthly. catches tokenization and beam-edge regressions.

michelle: on cost controls — tie full bench budget to model-size and commitment: tiny models (<6B) get auto-run; large models queue behind hourly slots unless a hard regression is detected.

perf-bot: [automation] scheduled bench job enqueued: model xg-2026-04, priority=low, scheduled=1748727000 :gear:

sara: final question — compatibility checks vs behavioral checks. we need both: binary/ABI sanity (onnx/torchscript shape, kv-cache offsets) plus behavior (golden/generative diffs). how do we order them?

dave: sanity/ABI checks first — they are cheap and fail-fast. then golden correctness + perf sampler. if ABI passes but golden flips, treat as behavioral regression and block. if only perf drift (no correctness flip) then can allow canary with throttled traffic and monitor.

michelle: one more ops thing — expose a small web UI in console to inspect the sampled long-tail bank for a model (search by input-hash) so SREs / ML eng can triage without backfilling. minimal columns: input-hash, sample-bucket, last-tested-commit, last-p95, repro-seed.

ben: +1 to UI. also log a compact signal to the rollout system so we can auto-pause rollouts that hit behavioral gates.

sara: great, thanks. I'll draft a short follow-up RFC with flow diagram, thresholds proposal, and the compact provenance schema. want volunteers to review — ada, ben, michelle?

ada: happy to.

ben: in.

michelle: yep, will make time this week.

perf-bot: [info] note: CI bench quota remaining for this week = 42 runs.
